self_review.toggle_label: Periodically re-check open investigations and parked actions
self_review.description: An investigation whose checks now read clean gets a closure proposal in the pending tray — approve it to actually close the investigation. A stuck "done, unverified" action is promoted to "done" automatically once its own checks re-verify clean (that's bookkeeping catching up to reality, not a new action); a pending proposal smith made on its own is superseded automatically once the condition it was about no longer applies.

self_review.never_run: No self-review sweep has run yet — runs automatically every 2h once smith is started.

brain_residency.description: Off (default): smith's brain is loaded on demand, only when a question actually needs the reasoning tier, and left to unload afterward per normal idle policy — no standing VRAM cost, but each first escalated question after an idle period pays a real load delay. On: smith proactively keeps the brain resident, permanently giving up its VRAM footprint in exchange for no per-question load latency. Either way, the brain is never pinned to a specific slot — the scheduler picks whichever is free.

autonomy.intro: Off by default. When enabled here, smith may carry out a specific, opted-in fix the moment it detects the problem — no click, no approval — instead of only ever proposing it for a human. Every autonomous run still goes through the same procedure engine (checkpoints, post-verify, full audit trail) as a manually-approved one, and is bounded by a cooldown plus a daily cap per procedure. Only procedures assessed as low-risk are ever eligible for this — the list below can't be widened from here.
autonomy.global_switch: Global switch — smith may run opted-in fixes unattended
autonomy.global_switch_note: The kill switch. Off always means nothing is autonomous, regardless of the per-procedure toggles below.
autonomy.none_eligible: No procedures are currently eligible for standing autonomy.

behavior.heading: Model Behavior
behavior.intro: A request's model name may resolve through an alias that forces its own defaults on every call through that name; capability-tier substitution (the toggle above) may then substitute an already-loaded config ranked in the same capability tier instead of waiting on a load; and reasoning_effort is translated per that config's own build — native passthrough where the build honors it directly, an injected enable_thinking kwarg where only that exists, or left alone where neither does. Mutations require admin + Settings assurance.
behavior.configs_note: One row per config. "native" under the thinking column means this build honors reasoning_effort directly and the override is unused; everything else is a build that only understands the enable_thinking chat-template kwarg (or nothing at all) — set Force on there to let reasoning_effort: none actually take effect on it.
behavior.tiers_note: Groups of configs that may substitute for each other under capability-tier substitution — an already-loaded model standing in for a requested one, to avoid a load wait or to prefer a smarter resident model. Curated, not derived: assign a config to a class and a rank (lower = more capable) in the table above or the config's own edit form. The global on/off mode is the Capability-tier substitution toggle on the Router behavior card above.
behavior.aliases_note: A second name for a config that FORCES a setting on every request through that name — even overriding what the caller asks for. For a consumer that can't send custom parameters itself (e.g. a fixed integration that can only be pointed at one model name), an alias guarantees the behavior it needs without a second, duplicate config.
behavior.virtual_models_note: A model name for a caller that doesn't care which real config serves it, only that it has some general characteristic — resolved to a real config fresh on every request, never a fixed target the way an alias is above. Capability-tier kind ranks a capability tier's own curated members; throughput kind ignores tiers entirely and ranks by real measured tokens/sec instead, so it's never a guess. Either way, whichever candidate is already loaded wins — otherwise the best-ranked one loads fresh, same as any other request.

routing.ensure_loaded_timeout_s.label: Ensure-loaded timeout
routing.ensure_loaded_timeout_s.help: How long a0 waits for an on-demand model load to finish before failing the request that triggered it.

routing.health_ttl_s.label: Health cache TTL
routing.health_ttl_s.help: How long a backend's health probe result is cached before a0 re-checks it.

routing.inject_stream_usage.label: Inject stream_options.include_usage
routing.inject_stream_usage.help: Ask remote providers for a trailing usage chunk on streaming requests, so real API spend can be recorded (BE-4 Phase 4). Local backends are unaffected.

routing.max_retries_per_backend.label: Max retries per backend
routing.max_retries_per_backend.help: How many times a0 retries a single backend before failing over or giving up.

routing.provider_failover.label: Provider failover
routing.provider_failover.help: When the preferred provider for a model errors (transport failure or 5xx), retry the next provider offering the same model, in priority order. Off = the error surfaces instead of silently spending on the next provider. 4xx responses never fail over.

routing.request_timeout_s.label: Request timeout
routing.request_timeout_s.help: 0 means unbounded — the deliberate default since the laguna-s-21 fix (2026-07-30): a flat non-zero timeout was severing long-running speculative-decode responses mid-generation. A hung client/upstream is still caught by context cancellation on disconnect.

routing.tts_url.label: TTS URL
routing.tts_url.help: Absolute http(s) URL for the forge-tts backend a0 proxies /v1/audio/speech and /v1/voices to (Tier 1 Sprint 3).

scheduling.seed.idle_unload_s.label: Idle unload (boot default)
scheduling.seed.idle_unload_s.help: Seed value sched.Config falls back to if scheduler.config has never been set. Writing this changes nothing on the running daemon — only what the next fresh boot starts from.

scheduling.seed.priority_jump_cap.label: Priority jump cap (boot default)
scheduling.seed.priority_jump_cap.help: Seed value for the priority jump cap — see idle unload above for what "boot default" means.

scheduling.seed.reservation_soon_min.label: Reservation-soon window (boot default)
scheduling.seed.reservation_soon_min.help: Seed value for the reservation-soon window — see idle unload above for what "boot default" means.

scheduling.seed.small_job_token_threshol.label: Small-job token threshold (boot default)
scheduling.seed.small_job_token_threshol.help: Seed value for the small-job token threshold — see idle unload above for what "boot default" means.

security.forward_auth.header_name.label: Forward-auth header name
security.forward_auth.header_name.help: HTTP header the reverse proxy sets with the authenticated username, when network_provider is forward_auth_header.

security.forward_auth.trusted_cidrs.label: Trusted CIDRs
security.forward_auth.trusted_cidrs.help: Comma-separated CIDR ranges allowed to set the forward-auth header. The highest-value check in this app: a save that would exclude YOUR OWN address is refused outright, not just warned about — total lockout is not recoverable without direct database access.

smith.brain_chain.label: smith brain fallback chain
smith.brain_chain.help: Ordered local configs smith tries when it needs to escalate to a brain — a loaded, idle member answers with zero load wait, otherwise smith falls down the chain toward smith.model.

smith.build_refresh_watchlist.label: build-refresh watchlist
smith.build_refresh_watchlist.help: Keywords smith matches against fetched upstream commit subjects when a tracked build has drifted — a hit is surfaced regardless of the drift threshold.

smith.handoff_offerings.label: smith handoff offering order
smith.handoff_offerings.help: Ordered remote Offerings smith's self-eviction handoff probes when its brain's slot needs to be freed.

smith.model.label: smith brain model
smith.model.help: The Config or Offering smith calls via a0 when it needs to think. Empty or unresolvable means smith answers without a model.

smith.schedule.deep.label: Deep sweep interval
smith.schedule.deep.help: How often smith runs its full check catalog, including slower network probes.

smith.schedule.quick.label: Quick sweep interval
smith.schedule.quick.help: How often smith runs its quick checks (a Go duration string, e.g. 60m).

smith.thresholds.build_refresh_behind_n.label: Build-refresh drift threshold
smith.thresholds.build_refresh_behind_n.help: How many commits a tracked build must drift behind upstream before smith proposes a rebuild. Below-threshold drift still shows as an info finding, it just doesn't propose a rebuild.

smith.thresholds.compressor_failopen_war.label: Compressor fail-open warn %
smith.thresholds.compressor_failopen_war.help: Fail-open rate threshold (%) — smith proposes raising the compressor fail-open budget when the 1-hour rolling rate exceeds this.

smith.thresholds.device_lost_window_minu.label: Device-lost detection window
smith.thresholds.device_lost_window_minu.help: How far back smith looks for a GPU device-lost event before treating it as resolved.

smith.thresholds.disk_crit_pct.label: Disk crit threshold
smith.thresholds.disk_crit_pct.help: Disk usage percentage at which smith's disk_space check reports crit.

smith.thresholds.disk_warn_pct.label: Disk warn threshold
smith.thresholds.disk_warn_pct.help: Disk usage percentage at which smith's disk_space check reports warn.

smith.thresholds.gtt_crit_pct.label: GTT crit threshold
smith.thresholds.gtt_crit_pct.help: GTT pool usage percentage at which smith's gtt_ceiling check reports crit.

smith.thresholds.gtt_warn_pct.label: GTT warn threshold
smith.thresholds.gtt_warn_pct.help: GTT pool usage percentage at which smith's gtt_ceiling check reports warn.

smith.web.api_keys.label: Web provider URLs and API keys
smith.web.api_keys.help: Base URLs and (optional) API keys for searxng and firecrawl.

smith.web.cache_ttl.label: Web cache TTL
smith.web.cache_ttl.help: How long a search or fetch result is reused before smith fetches it again (a Go duration string, e.g. 6h).

smith.web.enabled.label: Web research enabled
smith.web.enabled.help: Master switch for web research (search + fetch). On by default — turn off to keep smith to local evidence only.

smith.web.provider_order.label: Web provider order
smith.web.provider_order.help: Preference order among the fetch-capable adapters (searxng only searches; direct is always tried last regardless of this order).

voice.base.enabled.label: Base / clone: enabled
voice.base.enabled.help: Whether the Base / clone engine participates at all. Disabled refuses every request for it outright instead of silently falling back.

voice.base.mode.label: Base / clone: mode
voice.base.mode.help: Resident keeps the engine's systemd unit running continuously (fast, standing GPU memory). Available serves requests without a standing process (the existing CLI-reload-per-call fallback — kokoro has no such fallback tier, so available behaves the same as resident for it). Disabled refuses the engine outright.

voice.base.unit.label: Base / clone: systemd unit
voice.base.unit.help: The systemd unit this engine's resident process runs as (e.g. forge-tts-custom, kokoro). Empty means the daemon doesn't manage a process for it — resident mode then has nothing to start, same effect as available.

voice.base.url.label: Base / clone: backend URL
voice.base.url.help: Where forge-tts reaches this engine's resident backend (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8091). Empty means not configured — falls back to the CLI path for the three Qwen sub-variants, or is simply unreachable for kokoro.
